Build Medicare-primary coverage spells once, for repeated checks

Source: R/prepare_medicare_coverage.R
prepare_medicare_coverage.Rd

Keeps the payer history rows whose PAYER is one of payers and merges spans that touch or overlap, including a span nested inside an earlier one, into one spell per row. Pass the result to verify_medicare_primary() as medicare_coverage_df when it is called many times, for example once per risk set in a matching loop: prepared coverage is used as it is, while raw payer history is filtered and merged again on every call.

Usage

prepare_medicare_coverage(payhist, payers = c("MPAB", "MPO"))

Arguments

payhist

A data frame from the payhist file, with columns USRDS_ID, PAYER, BEGDATE and ENDDATE. BEGDATE and ENDDATE must be of class Date. PAYER may hold Appendix C $PAYCAT. codes or their labels.

payers

Payers whose spans make up the coverage, as Appendix C $PAYCAT. codes or their labels. The default, c("MPAB", "MPO"), is Medicare fee-for-service primary pay for both Part A and Part B, or "for other" (Appendix C $PAYCAT. labels): Medicare primary coverage (Researcher's Guide 2025, Example 8 and Section 4, Table 7). "MPAB" alone requires both parts. Secondary payer (MSP-EGHP, MSP-nonEGHP), HMO and WAIT spans are not Medicare primary, and claims are incomplete for them; see verify_medicare_primary().

Value

A data frame of class usrds_medicare_coverage, with one row per spell and columns USRDS_ID, BEGDATE and ENDDATE. Attributes record the payers used and the USRDS_IDs present in payhist, so verify_medicare_primary() can still warn about patients with no payer history at all. Patients with history but no eligible spell have no row.

Examples

payer_history <- data.frame(
  USRDS_ID = c(1, 1, 2),
  PAYER = c("MPAB", "MPAB", "MSP-EGHP"),
  BEGDATE = as.Date(c("2009-01-01", "2009-07-01", "2009-01-01")),
  ENDDATE = as.Date(c("2009-06-30", "2010-12-31", "2010-12-31"))
)
coverage <- prepare_medicare_coverage(payer_history)
coverage
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   USRDS_ID BEGDATE    ENDDATE   
#> *    <dbl> <date>     <date>    
#> 1        1 2009-01-01 2010-12-31

patients <- data.frame(
  USRDS_ID = c(1, 2),
  index = as.Date(c("2010-06-01", "2010-06-01"))
)
verify_medicare_primary(
  patients,
  index_date = "index",
  medicare_coverage_df = coverage
)
#>   USRDS_ID      index medicare_primary_TF
#> 1        1 2010-06-01                TRUE
#> 2        2 2010-06-01               FALSE
